name: bt4-vfs-packs
title: Build targets stage 4: virtual filesystem (folder, pack and bundle mounts), zip and 7z packs, user:// as today on desktop and web, the cook step
issue: User request, 2026-11-10: 'I would like for the engine to be able to allow the user to select a build target in the engine editor UI like windows, linux, android, ios, web, and maybe other console toolchains in the future like switch'. Design and stage table: orchestrator/proposals/build-targets-design.md. Stage 4 of section 5.
acceptance: Reads go through mounts; a project runs the same from a folder and from its pack (test)
The cook step runs the module-list check, writes the pack and a manifest of sizes and hashes
The web package carries the pack; web saves persist (IDBFS on user://) or the gap is documented
The audit of std::filesystem call sites is recorded in the design
The web package's size against its budget is measured and recorded; an uncompressed pack is allowed on the web if the reader's code costs more than it saves

Packs can be zip (default) or 7z, chosen per target; 7z packs are written non-solid (or in small solid blocks) so one file can be read without decompressing the rest; the reader is the LZMA SDK's 7z decoder
The reader's code size per target and the load times of zip and 7z packs are measured and recorded
gate: needs the user's go; depends on bt1-n2build-desktop-web; D6 decided: zip by default, 7z as an option
notes: Reviewer: no write outside user://, pack reads bounded and checked, path traversal out of a mount impossible.
